description:
**ABOUT QUINCE**

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world's finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

**OUR CULTURE**

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren't interested in replicating how others do retail. We're building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that's been done before.

* We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
* Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
* Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you're someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

**JOB TITLE****:**

**Manager. Material Production - Leather**

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Leather Inventory & Quality Control

* Oversee leather inventory levels to ensure adequate supply for tanning schedules while minimizing waste and overstock.
* Inspect and verify that only quality leather—meeting specified micron, length, and color consistency standards—is released into the tanning process.
* Implement checkpoints to catch non-conforming leather before production begins, preventing downstream defects.
* Coordinate with sourcing and warehouse teams to maintain accurate inventory records and proper storage conditions for raw leather.

  

On-Time Delivery (OTD) Management

* Own leather OTD performance, tracking delivery timelines from suppliers to tanneries and flagging potential delays.
* Proleatherly manage production schedules to ensure leather is available when needed, communicating risks to cross-functional partners.
* Resolve supply interruptions by expediting shipments or reallocating inventory as necessary to meet production deadlines.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for supplier lead times and delivery reliability.

  

Tanning & Production Support

* Partner with tanneries to ensure leather lots are processed according to technical specifications and quality expectations.
* Monitor leather consumption during tanning to identify discrepancies, yield loss, or quality deviations.
* Work upstream with suppliers to align leather bale composition, lot sizing, and traceability for smoother tannery integration.
* Maintain clear documentation of leather lots, test results, and production flow to support traceability and continuous improvement.

  

Cross-Functional Collaboration

* Coordinate with planners and production team to align leather availability with production demand and tanning schedules.
* Collaborate with R&D, Product Development, and Sourcing teams to support seamless production handoffs.
* Provide input on leather purchasing decisions based on production capacity, lead times, and quality performance history.
* Escalate production blockers (e.g., leather shortages, quality holds) with recommended solutions to meet OTD goals.

  

QUALIFICATIONS

* Education: Degree in Textile Engineering, Material Science, Supply Chain, or a related field.
* Production Experience: Proven experience managing raw materials in a textile or apparel production environment, preferably with leather or other luxury leathers.
* Quality Focus: Strong ability to assess leather quality and enforce standards before tanning.
* Inventory & OTD Acumen: Demonstrated skill in tracking inventory levels and driving on-time delivery performance.
* Analytical Skills: Ability to use data to monitor leather usage, identify yield issues, and improve production flow.
* Collaboration: Experience working with tanneries, suppliers, planners, and internal production teams to resolve issues quickly.

Preferred:

* Experience with leather leather grading, testing, or lot management.
* Knowledge of tannery operations and leather-to-yarn conversion.
* Familiarity with inventory management systems or ERP tools.
* Understanding of sustainable leather sourcing and production practices.

**WHY QUINCE?**

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

**What You'll Do:**

CoreWeave's Data Center Operations organization runs the physical infrastructure behind one of the world's leading AI cloud platforms: the GPU clusters that frontier AI labs and enterprises use to train and serve their models. As CoreWeave expands into Asia-Pacific, we're building a regional operations organization from the ground up. It will own uptime, safety, and operational excellence across every CoreWeave data center in the region, and set the standard for how we run at scale outside North America and Europe.

**About the Role:**

The Vice President, Data Center Operations – APAC is the senior operations leader for CoreWeave's Asia-Pacific data center portfolio, reporting directly to the SVP of Data Center Operations. You will own day-to-day operations across [Singapore, Korea, and future APAC sites]. This is a hands-on role: you'll be present in the data centers with your teams, not directing work from a distance. You'll build the regional team, put global standards and processes in place, and hold colocation partners, contractors, and vendors accountable to CoreWeave's performance bar. You'll work closely with global Operations, Fleet Operations, Engineering, Construction, Networking, and Supply Chain, as well as with executive leadership.

**In this role, you will:**

* Own operational performance for all APAC data centers (uptime, MTTR, safety, and audit readiness) and make the region a reliable, scalable part of CoreWeave's global fleet
* Build and lead the APAC operations organization (Regional/Area Managers, Data Center Managers, and Technicians), including hiring plans, leadership bench, and on-call coverage
* Adapt global SOPs, KPIs, and tooling for APAC, so that standards are followed consistently on site across countries and are not just documented
* Manage colocation partners, contractors, and vendors directly: drive schedule and SLA performance, escalate firmly, and decide when to course-correct or exit
* Lead new-site readiness and turn-up in partnership with Construction and Deployment, taking capacity from handoff to production on time
* Navigate local labor, regulatory, safety, and compliance requirements across multiple APAC jurisdictions
* Lead the response to critical (SEV-1) incidents in the region and represent APAC operations in executive reviews and global operating cadences

**Who You Are:**

* 15+ years in data center operations or critical infrastructure, including 5+ years leading multi-site operations at Senior Director/VP scope
* Proven ownership of live, production data center operations in APAC (operating sites, not only construction or project delivery) across more than one country
* Experience at a hyperscaler, large cloud provider, or major colocation/data center operator running high-density or mission-critical environments
* Track record of building and scaling operations teams of [XX+] people across multiple sites, including hiring and developing managers
* Hands-on experience managing colocation, facilities, and contractor relationships against SLAs, including performance management and commercial escalation
* Working knowledge of APAC labor law, regulatory, and EHS requirements across multiple jurisdictions (e.g., Singapore, India, Korea, Japan, Australia)
* Based in or willing to relocate to [Singapore or India], with frequent travel across the APAC region

**Preferred:**

* Experience running GPU/HPC or AI infrastructure at high rack density, including liquid cooling
* Experience standing up a new regional operations organization or market entry for a cloud or data center operator
* Familiarity with the Korean and/or Japanese data center markets
* Exposure to global operations standardization: SOP frameworks, KPI programs, and ticketing/DCIM tooling

description:
Key responsibilities

**1. Sourcing and procurement**

* Source titles against open UK orders from Amazon India and local Delhi suppliers, distributors and publishers (e.g. Atlantic, Biblia Impex, IBD, Asbookworld, My Book Shop).
* Pick the best source per title on price, availability, condition and delivery time; stay within the landed-cost limit set by the UK team.
* Place orders and make sure every invoice is raised to the company, not to an individual, so GST input credit can be claimed.
* Build and maintain supplier relationships; negotiate pricing and credit terms; add new suppliers and publishers as the catalogue grows.
* Keep a supplier scorecard covering price, fill rate, delivery time and condition quality.

**2. Receiving, QC and packing oversight**

* Receive supplier deliveries and reconcile them against the orders they were bought for.
* Direct the Packing & QC Associate's daily work and priorities.
* Make sure every book is graded against Amazon's condition guidelines before packing; return or claim on damaged, wrong or mismatched stock.
* Enforce the packing SOP (materials, box sizing, labelling) so parcels arrive in the UK in sellable condition.
* Keep packing materials in stock and reorder before they run out.

**3. Order tracking: received vs dispatched to UK**

* Own the daily order pipeline: received → sourced → in stock → QC passed → packed → shipped → delivered in the UK.
* Reconcile, every day, the UK orders received against what has been dispatched; chase every order stuck at any stage.
* Keep the tracking sheet / dashboard and the ShipStation workflow up to date so the UK team sees live status.
* Flag stock-outs, likely late orders and cancellations to the UK team early, with a proposed fix.

**4. Export logistics**

* Book courier pickups to the agreed consolidation schedule (e.g. 3x a week).
* Prepare export documents per shipment: commercial invoice, packing list, HS codes, CSB-IV/CSB-V shipping bills.
* Hand over and manifest parcels; track them through UK customs to delivery.
* Resolve customs holds, missing paperwork and delivery exceptions with the courier.
* Gather volume data to renegotiate courier rates as shipments grow.

**5. Compliance and administration**

* Maintain export records and GST input-credit records (packaging, freight, overheads).
* Send monthly data to the CA for GSTR-1 / GSTR-3B; track annual items such as LUT renewal, ROC and FEMA filings.
* Keep IEC, AD code, ICEGATE and courier KYC details current.
* Flag any capital movement or share allotment that needs an RBI (FC-GPR) filing.

**6. Cost, cash and reporting**

* Log per-shipment costs into the landed-cost model: book price, freight in, packing, freight out, overheads.
* Track supplier payments against funds received from ABN Hive; keep the petty-cash and expense log.
* Send a daily status update and a weekly report to the UK team (see below).

**7. Site and people**

* Run the site: stock layout, shelving, systems access, basic upkeep.
* Train, supervise and review the Packing & QC Associate; cover packing personally at peak times or absences.
